not_run.opus: Not run: the OpenRouter key had insufficient credit (HTTP 402 in the warm-up). 16 calls are reserved to add it to these exact puzzles with --append.
not_run.gemma: Free substitute for the frontier LLM. All 15 calls returned HTTP 429 (free endpoint rate-limited upstream), so it never made a move. Its 0% reflects rate limiting, not its cube skill.

meta.analysis: On this evidence, neither raw System-1 decision models nor an unmeasured frontier LLM should drive a cube agent alone. The three decision models answered in about 0.8-1.5 s per move but solved 0 of 9 puzzles. Jev and Clef fell into undo loops (U, U′, U, ...), and their confidences (0.003-0.47 across 18 options) were mostly low and never pointed toward progress. Luna refused 14 of 15 requests. No frontier or free LLM returned a single move (credit, reasoning cost and rate limits blocked all four attempts), so the frontier side is unmeasured. An exact search solved every puzzle optimally in milliseconds on the CPU. I would use a hybrid: deterministic search for the multi-step planning, and a fast decision model only for cheap, single-step classification and gating.
